goal: Define how an EVF invocation selects and enforces an unambiguous verification tier without confusing lifecycle layers or verifier stages.
original_intent: The user wants verification to be enforced whenever EVF is called at different levels.

context.name: Evolvable Validation Framework invocation enforcement
context.statement: One EVF call binds a requested verification tier to exact property traits, providers, evidence checks, bounds and claim limits.
context.provenance: Current user direction interpreted against existing TDE EVF L0/L1/L2 profiles, the Repair Assurance DAG and Auth S0-S12 enforcement profile.

consumer.intended_use: Input for a later governed Plan and separately authorized implementation of profile-driven verification enforcement.

goal_limits: no product, certification, publication, release or deployment effect

concepts.candidate_definition: A versioned additive set of minimum evidence, provider, control and review obligations that an EVF invocation must satisfy before asserting that tier.
A project-owned planning or delivery position such as Repair Assurance L2, L3 or L4; it does not select verifier obligations.
A provider or profile-owned execution checkpoint such as S0 through S12; stage completion alone does not name a verification tier.
A declared semantic dimension of the property that determines which verifier capabilities are applicable.
A verifier function such as Datalog fixed-point evaluation, relational model finding, temporal model checking, proof-kernel checking or executable evaluation, independent of one tool brand.
The result of checking whether all obligations for the requested tier were executed completely and truthfully.
Counterexample, no counterexample within bounds, inconclusive or conflicting evidence, derived separately from contract completion.
A new attributable caller selection of a lower verification tier after the requested tier could not be satisfied; never an automatic runtime fallback.

relationships: PropertyTrait requires one or more ProviderCapabilities at V3.
VerifierStage contributes evidence to a VerificationContractState.
VerificationContractState is evaluated independently of PropertyOutcome.
LifecycleLayer may request a VerificationTier but cannot redefine it.
allowed_uses: Review and refine verification-tier vocabulary and obligations.
Use as input to a separately routed EVF enforcement plan.
Design migration without rewriting historical evidence.
blocked_actions: Treat V0 through V4 as implemented runtime behavior.
Relabel historical L0/L1/L2 or S0-S12 receipts as verified tiers.
Silently downgrade an unsatisfied requested tier.
Treat complete verification as product approval or operational authority.
claim_ceiling: Defines candidate verification-tier semantics and migration constraints only; it does not enforce an invocation or establish any verified tier.

checks.detail: Verification tier, lifecycle layer and verifier stage are separately named.
Contract completion and property outcome are independent.
Tools are selected by declared property traits and provider capabilities.
No implementation, admission or external effect is granted.

open_questions_and_conflicts.question: Do two provider routes count as independent when they share one translation source?
Must V4 exercise a natural repair branch, or may a truthful no-counterexample result satisfy V4 with repair marked not applicable?
What exact compatibility record maps historical TDE levels and Auth stages without changing their claims?
